title: 400 people danced themselves to death — and nobody knows why
description:
In July 1518, a woman named Frau Troffea began dancing alone in a Strasbourg street. No music. No reason. She didn't stop. Within a week, dozens more joined her, feet bleeding, bodies collapsing from exhaustion.

City officials prescribed more dancing — building stages and hiring musicians. By August, over 400 people had joined the frenzied movement. Some accounts report 15 deaths a day from strokes, heart attacks, and sheer fatigue. The cure was the stage itself.

Modern theories point to ergot fungus, mass stress, and religious hysteria, but five centuries later, no explanation has ever been confirmed. What pulled all those people into the street remains a mystery.
